newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling gains further against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling gains further against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling firmed further on the dollar on Monday in an active market in which exporter sales put more pressure on the dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) posted a shilling mean rate of 56.47 against the dollar from 56.54 on Friday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.92 from 87.68 on Friday.
"The local market ended active last week firm against the dollar as exporter sales put further pressure on the dollar," a dealer said. "Opening trends reflected that mood."
"The market opened at 56.45/55 before dollar sales pushed it down to 56.33/43," she said. "As nervousness gripped the market, spreads widened and some players pulled off the market."
Another dealer added: "The central bank intervened at the 56.40 region (on Friday) sapping about $5 million from the market and pushing rates as high as 56.50/60."

"On Monday, however, sentiment for a stronger shilling prevailed and the market soon turned again to close at 56.40/50. We expect to see a further strengthening of the shilling this week," the dealer said.
Dealers said overnight money market rates edged up to above 20 percent levels as the market dried up.
